podcast.title: Approval of Kanye West Sampling
podcast.body: In stark contrast to Robert Fripp's strong disapproval, Greg Lake viewed Kanye West's sampling of King Crimson's first album's first track for the song "Power" as a "fantastic idea." He openly expressed feeling "truly flattered" that an artist as influential to young generations as Kanye West would utilize material he composed, and he was surprised by its enduring relevance nearly 50 years later. "Greg Lake que decía que se sentía verdaderamente alagado que alguien tan importante para la gente joven como Kanye West hubiese versionado a King Crimson a un material que le había compuesto."

podcast.title: Legacy as "True Genius" of First Album
podcast.body: Greg Lake was highly regarded as the "true genius" behind King Crimson's seminal first album. His death from cancer a few years prior further complicated Robert Fripp's already intricate efforts to manage the band's extensive catalog of rights. "él había sido el verdadero genio que estaba detrás del primer disco de King Crimson."

podcast.title: Protagonist of King Crimson's First Album
podcast.body: Greg Lake was considered the "true protagonist" of King Crimson's debut album, serving as both its singer and bassist. He was also credited as the author, or a primary author, of its most pivotal musical parts, which generated legal ambiguities regarding authorship with Robert Fripp. "Greg Lake... es el verdadero protagonista del primer risco de la banda. Era cantante, era bajo, pero también fue el autor de las partes más importantes en disco."
